title: Rosenlicht factorization of units on a product of integral varieties
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X,Y$ be nonempty integral separated schemes of finite type over $F$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. For every invertible regular function $u\in\Gamma(X\times_FY,\mathcal O)^\times$, there are $a\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times$ and $b\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)^\times$ such that $u=\operatorname{pr}_X^*a\,\operatorname{pr}_Y^*b$. An invertible regular function is a global section with a multiplicative inverse; equivalently it is a morphism to $\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. More precisely, for any $x_0\in X(F)$ and $y_0\in Y(F)$ there is an equality of regular functions $$u(x,y)=u(x,y_0)\,u(x_0,y)\,u(x_0,y_0)^{-1}.$$ The product is the scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Proposition 12.48, printed pp.246--247, especially identity (79); Remark 12.50, printed p.247. The statement concerns scheme fibre products, not cartesian products of rings.

proof.text:
Choose any prescribed $x_0\in X(F)$ and $y_0\in Y(F)$. Such points exist: the Jacobson-space lemma gives a closed point in any nonempty affine open of each scheme, and the closed-point residue-field lemma identifies its residue field with $F$. Set $c=u(x_0,y_0)\in F^\times$ and define the global unit
$$w=u\,c\,(\operatorname{pr}_X^*u(-,y_0))^{-1}(\operatorname{pr}_Y^*u(x_0,-))^{-1}.$$
Pullback is a ring map, so all factors are units. Direct cancellation gives $w(x,y_0)=1$ and $w(x_0,y)=1$ as regular functions on the two slices.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, pp.246--247, identity (79); agent-written affine bounded-inverse proof of the same normalization identity, instead of the printed boundary-divisor proof.

proof.text: Use the finite-type affine covers to choose $x_0\in U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and $y_0\in T=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ with $A,B$ finitely generated $F$-algebras. Both are domains by integrality. By the open-fibre-product lemma, $U\times_F T$ is the open subscheme $\operatorname{pr}_X^{-1}(U)\cap\operatorname{pr}_Y^{-1}(T)$ of $X\times_FY$, compatibly with the projections, so $w$ and $w^{-1}$ restrict to it. The affine fibre-product theorem identifies $\Gamma(U\times_F T,\mathcal O)$ with $A\otimes_F B$, including both projection maps. Write the restrictions of $w$ and $w^{-1}$ as finite sums of pure tensors. Let $V,W\subseteq A$ be the spans of their respective first coordinates. For every $y\in T(F)$, evaluation on the second tensor coordinate gives $w_y\in A^\times$ with $w_y\in V$ and $w_y^{-1}\in W$. The bounded-inverse unit-lines lemma gives finitely many possibilities for $F w_y$. Since $w_y(x_0)=1$, each such line has at most one representative occurring among these $w_y$. Thus the set of sections $w_y$ itself is finite and nonempty; denote its distinct members by $f_1,\ldots,f_s$.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, pp.246--247, identity (79); agent-written affine bounded-inverse proof of the same normalization identity, instead of the printed boundary-divisor proof.

proof.text: Choose a basis $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $V$ and write $w=\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i$ and $f_j=\sum_i c_{ij}a_i$, with $b_i\in B$ and $c_{ij}\in F$. Put $I_j=(b_i-c_{ij})_i\subseteq B$. For every $y\in T(F)$, the equality $w_y=f_j$ for some $j$ says $I_j$ vanishes at $y$, by independence of the $a_i$. If every $I_j$ were nonzero, choose $0\ne h_j\in I_j$. The product $\prod_j h_j$ would vanish at every $F$-point of $T$, hence be zero by the affine Nullstellensatz vanishing principle, contradicting that $B$ is a domain. Consequently some $I_j=0$. Then $w=f_j\otimes1$; evaluation at $y_0$ and $w(-,y_0)=1$ give $f_j=1$. Hence $w=1$ on $U\times_F T$.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, pp.246--247, identity (79); agent-written affine bounded-inverse proof of the same normalization identity, instead of the printed boundary-divisor proof.

proof.text: For each $y\in T(F)$, the global section $w(-,y)-1$ on $X$ restricts to zero on $U$. Its germ in the function field is therefore zero, so injectivity of sections into the function field gives $w(-,y)=1$ on all of $X$. Now fix any $x\in X(F)$. The section $w(x,-)-1$ on $Y$ vanishes at every $F$-point of $T$, so its restriction to the reduced affine $T$ is zero by the affine vanishing principle. Injectivity into the function field of $Y$ then gives $w(x,-)=1$ globally. Thus $w(x,y)=1$ for all $(x,y)\in X(F)\times Y(F)$.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, pp.246--247, identity (79); agent-written affine bounded-inverse proof of the same normalization identity, instead of the printed boundary-divisor proof.

proof.text: Let $P=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $Q=\operatorname{Spec}D$ range through finite-type affine covers of $X$ and $Y$. By the open-fibre-product lemma each $P\times_FQ$ is the open subscheme $\operatorname{pr}_X^{-1}(P)\cap\operatorname{pr}_Y^{-1}(Q)$ of $X\times_FY$, compatibly with the projections. These products cover $X\times_FY$: any point belongs to the intersection of the inverse images of one such $P$ and one such $Q$. On $P\times_F Q$, write $w-1=\sum_i e_i\otimes d_i\in C\otimes_F D$ with the finitely many $e_i$ linearly independent, collecting coefficients in a basis of their span. For any $y\in Q(F)$, the element $\sum_i d_i(y)e_i\in C$ vanishes at every $x\in P(F)$, by the preceding step. The affine vanishing principle on the reduced ring $C$ makes it zero, and independence gives $d_i(y)=0$ for every $i$. The same principle on the reduced ring $D$ gives $d_i=0$. Hence $w-1=0$ on every product chart, and by the sheaf axiom $w=1$ globally.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, pp.246--247, identity (79); agent-written affine bounded-inverse proof of the same normalization identity, instead of the printed boundary-divisor proof.

proof.text:
Expanding $w=1$ and multiplying by its unit denominators yields
$$u(x,y)=u(x,y_0)u(x_0,y)c^{-1}.$$
Take $a=u(-,y_0)$ and $b=u(x_0,-)c^{-1}$. These are global units, since they are pullbacks of the unit $u$ times a nonzero scalar. The displayed equality is $u=\operatorname{pr}_X^*a\operatorname{pr}_Y^*b$. The construction began with arbitrary prescribed basepoints, so it proves the asserted identity for every pair of basepoints.

The item's hypotheses (integral, separated, finite type over algebraically closed F) match Milne's irreducible varieties, and the statement changed only in its TeX escapes. The arbitrary-basepoint identity is correct. Read the agent-written affine proof step by step. Step 1: slice normalization w with w(x,y0)=1 and w(x0,y)=1, using jacobson-space and closed-point-residue-field. Step 2: on A⊗B, w_y lies in V and its inverse in W; the new lemma bounds the lines, and w_y(x0)=1 makes the set {w_y} finite. Step 3: coefficient ideals I_j; if all were nonzero, the product of nonzero elements would vanish on T(F), which Nullstellensatz clause 2 and the domain hypothesis forbid; so w=f_j⊗1=1. Step 4: generic-germ injectivity (clause 1 of integral-scheme-stalks) plus Nullstellensatz give w=1 on X(F)×Y(F). Step 5: chartwise two-variable vanishing and the sheaf axiom. Step 6: cancellation. All of this is correct. New node lem-sfb-bounded-inverse-unit-lines is true and self-contained. lean.statement: theorem rosenlicht_product_unit_factorization (F : Type u) [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of F)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of F)) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsSeparated f] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] (u : (Γ(pullback f g, ⊤))ˣ) : (∃ (a : (Γ(X, ⊤))ˣ) (b : (Γ(Y, ⊤))ˣ), u = Units.map (pullback.fst f g).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a * Units.map (pullback.snd f g).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom b) ∧ (∀ (x₀ : Spec (.of F) ⟶ X) (y₀ : Spec (.of F) ⟶ Y) (hx : x₀ ≫ f = 𝟙 (Spec (.of F))) (hy : y₀ ≫ g = 𝟙 (Spec (.of F))), u = Units.map (pullback.fst f g).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom (Units.map (rosenlichtSliceX f g y₀ hy).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom u) * Units.map (pullback.snd f g).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom (Units.map (rosenlichtSliceY f g x₀ hx).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom u) * Units.map (pullback.fst f g ≫ f).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom ((Units.map (x₀ ≫ rosenlichtSliceX f g y₀ hy).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom u)⁻¹))
